Viele Unternehmen organisieren ihre Tagungen, Meetings & Events noch immer komplex, intransparent und ineffizient. Genau hier kommen wir ins Spiel.


Mit unserer SaaS-Lösung digitalisieren und vereinfachen wir den gesamten Einkaufsprozess rund um Business Events – von der Anfrage bis zur Abwicklung.


Und genau dafür suchen wir Dich: jemanden, der nicht nur verkauft, sondern versteht, strukturiert denkt und Kunden wirklich weiterbringt.


Deine Rolle

Als Account Executive im Enterprise Sales verantwortest Du komplexe Deals von der ersten Hypothese bis zum Abschluss.
Du verstehst Kundenbedürfnisse und entwickelst daraus überzeugende Lösungen – ideal, um Deine analytischen Skills einzusetzen.

Konkret bedeutet das:

  • Du identifizierst und entwickelst neue Enterprise-Kunden und baust Dir eine eigene Pipeline auf
  • Du analysierst Kundenanforderungen und entwickelst strukturierte, überzeugende Lösungen
  • Du erstellst starke Präsentationen für verschiedene Stakeholder bis hin zum C-Level
  • Du steuerst komplexe Entscheidungsprozesse und moderierst unterschiedliche Interessen
  • Du verantwortest Deals end-to-end – von Angebot bis Abschluss inkl. Verhandlung
  • Du arbeitest eng mit Produkt, Marketing und Customer Success zusammen

  • Du hältst Deine Pipeline sauber und Deinen Forecast belastbar im CRM


Was uns gefällt

Wir suchen keine perfekte Sales-Vita – sondern die richtigen Skills und das richtige Mindset.

  • Du hast Erfahrung in einem strukturierten, anspruchsvollen Umfeld (z. B. Beratung, SaaS oder B2B)
  • Du denkst analytisch, strukturierst komplexe Themen klar und präsentierst überzeugend
  • Du bewegst Dich sicher im Austausch mit verschiedenen Stakeholdern
  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, strukturiert und behältst auch in komplexen Prozessen den Überblick
  • Du hast Lust, Verantwortung für Deals und echten Business Impact zu übernehmen
  • Erste Vertriebserfahrung und CRM-Kenntnisse sind ein Plus
  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch


Was Dir gefällt

  • Du bist Teil eines motivierten und hochqualifizierten Teams mit flachen Hierarchien und – Überraschung – regelmäßigen Teamevents, wie z.B. Afterwork Drinks auf der Dachterrasse, Culture Nights, Spieleabende oder unsere Teamevents am Monatsende, bei denen wir uns gemeinsam pushen die letzten Abschlüsse reinzuholen und unsere Erfolge feiern
  • Sei ein Sparfuchs und nutze Prozente auf diverse Marken und Reisen durch PepXpress und Corporate Benefits
  • Natürlich gibt es auch den obligatorischen Obstkorb, eine Müslibar sowie kalte und warme Getränke
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten. Das sieht in jedem Team unterschiedlich aus. Grundsätzlich gelten die Kernarbeitszeiten von 10 - 17 Uhr
  • Du hast Lust, mit Blick auf die Elbe und einige der bekanntesten und schönsten Sehenswürdigkeiten Hamburgs zu arbeiten?
  • Du entscheidest, welche Benefits zu Dir passen: mit 20€ Benefitsy, 20€ Zuschuss zum DEU-Ticket oder 20€ Zuschuss für Urban Sports
  • Wir fördern Deine individuelle Weiterentwicklung mit dem Learning Budget von 300€ pro Jahr
  • Oben drauf packen wir noch monatlich bis zu 100€ für Deine Altersvorsorge und Vermögensziele (bAV und VWL)


Deine Ansprechpartnerin

Hellen, unsere Talent Acquisition Managerin

data.description:
Einleitung

Willst Du während Deines Studiums nicht nur Theorie büffeln, sondern von Tag eins an echte Verantwortung im Finance-Bereich eines wachsenden Scale-ups übernehmen? Dann bist Du bei uns genau richtig!

Peter Park digitalisiert das Parken: Mit automatischer Kennzeichenerkennung (ALPR) und einer cloudbasierten Management-Software machen wir Parkscheine, Schranken und Parkscheiben überflüssig. Deine Mission als Werkstudent:in Finance & Controlling: Du unterstützt unser Finance-Team im Tagesgeschäft und bei den Abschlüssen – und hilfst mit, wiederkehrende manuelle Prozesse mit modernen KI-Tools zu vereinfachen und zu automatisieren. Du arbeitest eng mit dem Finance-Team zusammen und übernimmst von Anfang an eigene Aufgaben und Projekte, an denen Du wachsen kannst.


Was ist Deine Aufgabe?


  • Abschlussarbeiten: Du unterstützt bei der Vorbereitung von Monats- und Jahresabschlüssen.

  • Buchhaltung & Zahlungsverkehr: Du übernimmst Buchungen (u. a. in DATEV) und unterstützt bei der laufenden Zahlungsabwicklung.

  • Rechnungsstellung: Du erstellst, prüfst und versendest Rechnungen und Gutschriften – inklusive Pflege der zugehörigen Kostenstellen-, Konten- und Lieferantendaten in Excel und HubSpot.

  • Digitalisierung & KI: Du arbeitest an Digitalisierungs- und Automatisierungsprojekten mit, hinterfragst wiederkehrende manuelle Prozesse im Finance-Bereich aktiv und bringst eigene Ideen ein, wie sich diese z. B. mit KI-Tools vereinfachen lassen.

  • Datenpflege & -analyse: Du unterstützt bei der Datenpflege und -analyse, u. a. bei länderspezifischen Auswertungen und Datenimporten.

  • Kommunikation: Du übernimmst die Korrespondenz mit Kund:innen und Lieferant:innen und unterstützt im operativen Tagesgeschäft.

  • Cross-funktionale Projekte: Du arbeitest an abteilungsübergreifenden Projekten mit.


Deine Fähigkeiten:


  • Studium: Du studierst Finance, BWL, VWL oder einen vergleichbaren Studiengang.

  • Praxis-Basics: Rechnungserstellung, Kontierungen und Soll-Ist-Vergleiche sind Dir nicht fremd.

  • Arbeitsweise: Du arbeitest strukturiert, detailorientiert und zuverlässig.

  • Tools: Du bist sicher im Umgang mit MS Office, insbesondere Excel und PowerPoint.

  • Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

  • Mindset: Hohe Eigenmotivation, Zahlenaffinität und eine offene, kommunikative Persönlichkeit zeichnen Dich aus.

  • KI-Affinität: Du hast bereits mit gängigen KI-Tools wie Claude, Gemini oder ChatGPT gearbeitet und hast Lust, damit Finance-Prozesse smarter zu machen.


Work Setup:


  • Werkstudierendenvertrag – befristet auf die Dauer Deines Studiums

  • Bis zu 20 Stunden pro Woche während der Vorlesungszeit, in den Semesterferien bis zu 40 Stunden pro Woche

  • Hybrides Arbeiten mit der Möglichkeit, zeitweise remote innerhalb der EU zu arbeiten

  • Arbeitsort: München (Neue Balan), Team: 8 Kolleg:innen


Welche Vorteile bietet mir Peter Park?

So sieht Dein Arbeitsalltag bei uns aus

  • Arbeiten mit Bergblick: Unser Büro in der Neuen Balan bietet mehr als nur moderne Ausstattung: Von der Dachterrasse aus genießt Du ein Alpenpanorama, im Sommer wird gemeinsam gegrillt, und unsere Teamevents sorgen für gute Stimmung.

  • Teamgeist und Impact-Kultur: Bei uns zählt Deine Stimme! Wir leben flache Hierarchien und eine Kultur des "Du" vom ersten Tag an. Das bedeutet: kurze Entscheidungswege, direkter Austausch mit allen Ebenen und ein Team, das Dich aktiv unterstützt. Deine Ideen sind hier nicht nur willkommen, sondern werden gehört.

  • Freiraum für Deine Ideen: Du übernimmst Verantwortung und kannst Deine Ideen aktiv einbringen. Wir fördern Deine Entwicklung – mit echtem Vertrauen in Deine Fähigkeiten.

Das bieten wir Dir zusätzlich

  • Dein Plus: Rabatte bei zahlreichen Marken über unser Corporate-Benefits-Programm und on top wählst du selbst zwischen einem bezuschussten Deutschlandticket oder EGYM Wellpass

  • Deine Flexibilität: 20 Urlaubstage (anteilig berechnet auf Deine tatsächlichen Arbeitstage), flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit, zeitweise remote innerhalb der  EU zu arbeiten. In den Semesterferien hast Du außerdem die Möglichkeit, Vollzeit mit bis zu 40 Std./Woche voll durchzustarten.

  • Dein Setup: Ein Onboarding, das dich direkt abholt, höhenverstellbare Tische und modernes Apple Equipment für deinen perfekten Start ab Tag eins

  • Dein Wohlbefinden: Ein gesunder Energiekick durch kostenlose Snacks (Obst, Nüsse, Müsli), bezuschusstes Office-Catering und der wöchentliche, kostenlose Team-Lunch

✅ Bereit für den nächsten Schritt?

Dann werde Teil unseres Teams – und gestalte mit uns die Zukunft! Bewirb Dich einfach und schnell über den Button unten "Auf diese Stelle bewerben" Wir freuen uns, von Dir zu hören!

Einleitung

Schranken, Papiertickets, Parkscheiben – das war gestern. Heute bauen wir smarte Mobility Hubs, morgen die größten Enterprise-Deals der Parkbranche. Dafür suchen wir keinen Farmer, der bestehende Accounts hegt, sondern einen echten Hunter: Als eine:r unserer ersten Senior Account Executives im brandneuen Enterprise-Team baust Du unsere Enterprise-Sales-Motion in Deutschland komplett neu auf: Zielaccounts, Ansprache-Strategie, erster unterschriebener Vertrag, alles mit Deiner Handschrift. Im Zentrum steht eine klar definierte Named Account List (NAL) der wichtigsten Enterprise-Player Deutschlands, zu denen Du Dir proaktiv den Weg zu den relevanten Entscheider:innen bahnst, Hand in Hand mit unserem Marketing-Team und dessen ABM-Kampagnen. Du arbeitest eng mit unserer Geschäftsführung, unserem VP Sales sowie unserem neuen Head of Enterprise Sales zusammen.


Was ist Deine Aufgabe?

  • Du baust die Enterprise-Sales-Motion in Deutschland von null auf. Prozesse, Ansprache-Strategie und Playbooks entstehen mit Dir.

  • Du entwickelst und bespielst unsere Named Account List (NAL) und verschaffst Dir über Multi-Threading Zugang zu allen relevanten Entscheider:innen.

  • Du gehst outbound first auf Kundenjagd: Kaltakquise, Netzwerken, Events, gemeinsame ABM-Kampagnen mit Marketing. Leads wartest Du nicht ab, Du machst sie.

  • Du verantwortest den gesamten Sales-Cycle: von Video-Call und Vor-Ort-Demo bis Vertragsabschluss und Übergabe an unser Operations-Team.

  • Du berätst bis auf C-Level zu Verträgen, Technik, Mobilitätskonzepten, Ausschreibungen und Partnerschaften und gibst Kundenfeedback direkt an unser Produkt-Team weiter.

  • Du baust gemeinsam mit Geschäftsführung, VP Sales und Head of Enterprise Sales das Team auf und coachst künftig auch (Junior) Account Executives.

  • Du repräsentierst Peter Park bei strategischen Terminen und Branchenevents.


Deine Fähigkeiten:

  • Waschechter Hunter & Connector: Beziehungen auf allen Ebenen aufbauen ist für Dich kein Aufwand, sondern Hobby. Du bist pragmatisch und street smart.

  • Riesige Resilience: Lange Sales-Cycles und Rückschläge spornen Dich an, statt Dich zu bremsen.

  • Senior Room Presence: Vorstandsetagen sind für Dich Wohnzimmer, nicht Bühnenangst.

  • Influencer & Persuader: Du überzeugst mit Substanz und Charisma, nicht mit Druck.

  • Komplexität schreckt Dich nicht, sie reizt Dich. Du schneidest Dich durch wie ein heißes Messer durch Butter.

  • Nachgewiesene quantitative Erfolgsbilanz im Knacken von Quotas und Greenfield-Territorien. Net-New-Logos statt warmer Leads. Top-Performer-Auszeichnungen? Gerne erzählen.

  • Sattelfest in MEDDIC/MEDDPICC, Challenger Sale & Co., mit einer CRM-Pipeline, die nicht lügt (Hubspot, Salesforce).

  • 5+ Jahre B2B-Vertrieb, idealerweise mit Enterprise-/Named-Account-Erfahrung; Erfahrung mit Hardware+Software-Lösungen (IoT, Sensorik) ist ein Plus, kein Muss.

  • Erfahrung mit Account-Based Marketing oder enger Zusammenarbeit mit Marketing-Teams an Zielaccount-Strategien.

  • Unternehmerischer Kopf, der mit Ambiguität tanzt statt zu zögern. Ein Studium ist nett, aber kein Muss.

  • Fließend Deutsch, sehr gutes Englisch. 



Work Setup:

  • 40 Stunden/Woche (Vertrauensbasis)

  • Arbeitsort: München (3 Tage Office / 2 Tage remote) oder 100 % remote (deutschlandweit) mit regelmäßigen Trips ins Büro nach München. 

  • Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag

  • Reisebereitschaft: ca. 50 % (deutschlandweit) für Termine mit Deinen Target Accounts

  • Neu aufgebautes Enterprise-Team. Du gehörst zu den Ersten

  • Reporting an unseren neuen Head of Sales, Enterprise


Welche Vorteile bietet mir Peter Park?

So ticken wir! Passt das zu Dir?

  • Own & Prioritize: „Nicht mein Job“ gibt's bei uns nicht. Du übernimmst und ziehst durch.

  • Think Big: Wir denken in Portfolios, nicht in Einzeldeals.

  • Bias for Action: Wir entscheiden schnell und justieren im Gehen nach.

  • Have Backbone, Disagree & Commit: Du sagst früh, was Du denkst und ziehst mit, wenn entschieden ist.


Du erfüllst nicht jeden einzelnen Punkt auf dieser Liste, brennst aber für diese Rolle? Bewirb Dich trotzdem – wir schätzen Persönlichkeit und Lernbereitschaft mindestens so sehr wie einen perfekten Lebenslauf.

Deine Vorteile

  • Vertrauensbasiertes, flexibles Arbeiten im Office mit Alpenblick in der neuen Balan oder remote.

  • Start-up-Flair trotz Wachstumstempo: kurze Wege, Duz-Kultur vom Werksstudent bis zum CEO.

  • Attraktives Fixgehalt plus leistungsbasierter Bonus.

  • Eigenverantwortung, Feedback-Kultur, steile Lernkurve und die Chance, eine ganze Enterprise-Motion von Grund auf mitzugestalten.

  • 29 Urlaubstage, Team-Events, IT-Ausstattung Deiner Wahl, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Urban Sports Club, Essenszuschuss, wöchentlicher Team-Lunch.

  • EU-Workation: Du kannst auch mal von einem anderen EU-Land aus arbeiten.


Klingt nach Dir? Schick uns Deine Bewerbung an ----- – wir freuen uns auf Dich!

data.description:
Tiermedizin neu gedacht - mit dir!

Rex hat es sich zur Aufgabe gemacht, Tierhalter:innen dabei zu helfen, sich optimal um ihre besten Freunde kümmern zu können.
Um dies zu erreichen, wollen wir die tierärztliche Versorgung von Grund auf neu gestalten, wobei wir uns zum einen auf die Zufriedenheit und die Entwicklung unserer Mitarbeitenden im Team und zum anderen auf ein verbessertes Kundenerlebnis konzentrieren.
Bei uns wird Deine Stimme nicht nur gehört, sondern wir brauchen Deine Erfahrung und Deine Perspektive, um Rex noch schneller weiter wachsen zu lassen.


Warum bei Rex? Ganz einfach:

Wir stellen uns der komplexen Herausforderung, die Veterinärmedizin digital zu transformieren. Dafür entwickeln und betreiben wir eine hochverfügbare, skalierbare Plattform, die sowohl eine herausragende Customer Experience als auch effiziente, datengestützte Praxisabläufe ermöglicht.

Da wir kontinuierlich neue Praxen eröffnen und unsere Präsenz in Deutschland ausbauen, suchen wir jemanden, der sicherstellt, dass jeder neue Standort ab Tag 1 technisch startklar ist – und dass die Infrastruktur hinter unserer Plattform mit unserem Wachstum sicher und stabil bleibt. Baue und betreue die Systeme, die unsere Expansion erst möglich machen!


Spannende Aufgaben warten auf Dich:

Als unser IT System Engineer sorgst Du für verlässliche Systeme und treibst exzellente Prozesse in folgenden Bereichen voran:

  • Praxis-Infrastruktur & Setups: 
    Du planst und setzt das komplette IT-Setup bei Neueröffnungen um – von der IT-Beschaffung, dem Netzwerkdesign und der VPN-Anbindung an zentrale Systeme über die Bereitstellung von Workstations, POS-Kassen, Druckern und Peripherie bis hin zur Einrichtung und Fehlersuche bei medizinischen Geräten. Vor dem Go-Live validierst Du, dass alles reibungslos funktioniert.

  • Laufender Praxis-Support: 
    Du leistest Troubleshooting und Hardware-Support für unser wachsendes Praxisnetzwerk und entwickelst standardisierte, wiederholbare Setup-Prozesse, die mit jeder Eröffnung schneller und zuverlässiger werden.

  • Cloud-Infrastruktur & Security: 
    Du verwaltest und entwickelst unsere Cloud-Umgebung weiter und verantwortest das Sicherheits- und Zugriffsmanagement (IAM-Richtlinien, Credential Hygiene, Least-Privilege-Prinzip). Im Zuge unserer Skalierung hilfst Du uns, die nächste Stufe der Infrastruktur-Reife einzuführen (z. B. Load Balancing und automatisiertes Infrastruktur-Management).

  • Compliance & Datenschutz: 
    Du stellst sicher, dass unsere Infrastruktur und Praxis-Setups allen Datenschutzanforderungen (inkl. DSGVO/GDPR) beim Umgang mit Kunden- und Patientendaten entsprechen – von Zugriffskontrollen vor Ort bis hin zu Speicherung, Absicherung und Auditierung in der Cloud.

  • Monitoring & Reliability: 
    Du überwachst die Verfügbarkeit und Performance unserer Systeme, nimmst an Rotationen teil und erkennst Infrastrukturrisiken, bevor sie zu Ausfällen werden.

  • Engineering-Partnerschaft: 
    Du arbeitest bei Deployments und Infrastruktur-Anforderungen eng mit unserem Software-Engineering-Team zusammen und bringst ein operatives Mindset in die Entwicklung und den Release-Prozess ein.


Du verfügst über folgende Qualifikationen:

Wir suchen IT Sytem Engineers, die sich sowohl im praktischen Hardware-Handling als auch im Cloud-Betrieb zu Hause fühlen – pragmatische Problemlöser statt Theoretiker, die nur an einer Ebene des Stacks arbeiten wollen.

  • Standort & Sprache: 
    Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. Ein aktueller Wohnsitz in Deutschland sowie eine gültige Arbeitserlaubnis sind zwingende Voraussetzung für diese Rolle.

  • Reisebereitschaft: 
    Bereitschaft (20%) zu gelegentlichen Dienstreisen zu unseren Praxisstandorten.

  • Erfahrung & Ownership: 
    Mindestens 4 Jahre praktische Erfahrung in der IT-Systemadministration, im Infrastructure Engineering oder einer vergleichbaren hybriden Rolle. Nachweisbare Fähigkeit, Infrastrukturprojekte eigenverantwortlich von der Planung über die Umsetzung bis zum Support zu steuern.

  • Erforderliche technische Kenntnisse:

    • Netzwerk: Solide Grundlagen (TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, Firewalls, WLAN-Konfiguration) sowie Praxiserfahrung in der Anbindung von Standorten/Filialen.

    • Cloud: Hands-on-Erfahrung mit mindestens einem gängigen Cloud-Provider (z. B. AWS, DigitalOcean).

    • Security: Praktische Erfahrung mit Cloud-Sicherheit und Access Management (IAM, Secrets Management, Audit-Grundlagen).

  • Core Engineering Practices: 
    Erfahrung mit Rufbereitschaften (On-Call) und Incident Response sowie ein ausgeprägter Instinkt bei der Fehlersuche über Physische- und Cloud-Systeme hinweg.

Wir wissen, dass man nicht immer alle Kriterien erfüllen kann. Trotzdem würden wir uns freuen von dir zu hören, wenn du denkst, dass du genau der/die Richtige für die Rolle bist!


Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig!

Wir haben es uns zum Ziel gesetzt, Barrieren und Diskriminierung zu beseitigen und Chancengleichheit durch unser transparentes Einstellungsverfahren zu gewährleisten. Wir sind offen für alle Personengruppen ohne Rücksicht auf Alter, Hautfarbe, nationale Herkunft, Rasse, Religion, Geschlecht, sexuelle Orientierung, Geschlechtsidentität und/oder -ausdruck, Familienstand oder andere Merkmale.

data.description:
About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

1,000+ customers across 50+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $100M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI and Graceview.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

About the Role


The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an experienced Engagement Manager to own Legora's global relationship with one of the Big 4, one of our most significant partnerships, and to fundamentally change the way that firm works with Legora.

This is a role for someone who has led change inside large, complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed. You will own the adoption and long-term success of this client globally: building the relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser and orchestrator who turns Legora into an embedded part of how their teams operate.

Global means global. You will set the strategy for how the firm adopts Legora worldwide,and Engagement Managers in other regions will run their local programmes against the direction and decisions you set. Day to day, you will be the point of contact for the firm's UK and Ireland practice from our London office, and you will travel regularly to other
member firms in the network to build those relationships and land the programme on the ground. Expect to be travelling around 25% of the time.

At the heart of the role is designing the client's adoption playbook and delivering a multi-year change-management programme that transforms how they work. You will build the roadmap, sequence initiatives from initial rollout through firm-wide scaled adoption,define measurable outcomes and ROI and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge.

You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class adoption programme at Legora, helping the client realise measurable ROI, expand successful use cases and transform the way their teams work.

What You'll Do


You'll own the global relationship end to end, leading the post-sale experience across every member firm we work with. Specifically, you will:


● Set the global adoption strategy for the account and lead its execution across regions. Engagement Managers in other markets will deliver their local programmes against the strategy and decisions you set, and you will be accountable for coherence and outcomes globally.
● Act as the primary point of contact for the firm's UK and Ireland practice, while travelling frequently to other member firms to build senior relationships and support local delivery in person.
● Design the client's adoption playbook: the tailored change-management approach, stakeholder map and target outcomes for how the firm adopts Legora and transforms the way it works.

data.description:
About Stora

Stora is building the operating platform for modern self-storage businesses.

Our software helps operators manage bookings, payments, customers, facilities and day-to-day operations from one place, while automating much of the work that traditionally makes running a self-storage business unnecessarily complicated.

In just over five years, Stora has grown from an early-stage product into a platform used by more than 500 operators.

We’re a product-led, remote-first company with an experienced engineering team and ambitious plans for what comes next.

Now, as the engineering organisation grows, we’re hiring an Engineering Manager to make sure the way we lead, develop and support engineers grows with it.

The Role

This is a genuine people leadership role.

You’ll manage approximately 12 engineers working across three product teams, with the team expected to continue growing.

Each product team has a Tech Lead responsible for technical direction, alongside Product and Design. Your focus is different: the engineers themselves.

This isn’t a role for somebody looking to move away from engineering completely, though. You’ll need enough technical depth to understand the work, follow engineering discussions and ask good questions without needing to be the person making every technical decision.

You’ll work closely with our Head of Engineering and have support from People, but you’ll have meaningful autonomy to improve how engineering management works at Stora.

What Else You’ll Own

Engineering Management

  • Manage engineers across multiple product teams through regular, useful 1:1s, coaching and clear feedback.

  • Make expectations clear and help engineers understand what good performance looks like.

  • Identify performance issues early and handle difficult conversations properly when needed.

  • Support engineers in progressing from junior through senior and beyond.

  • Build strong relationships with engineers without creating unnecessary management overhead.

Performance & Progression

  • Own the engineering performance and progression approach.

  • Review and improve our existing career levels, expectations and review processes.

  • Make promotion and progression decisions that are consistent, evidence-based and understood by the team.

  • Create a culture where feedback happens throughout the year rather than being saved for formal reviews.

Hiring & Team Development

  • Own engineering hiring alongside the relevant Tech Leads and wider team.

  • Help define what we need before a search begins, assess candidates properly and maintain a high hiring bar.

  • Ensure new engineers have a structured and useful onboarding experience.

  • Think proactively about team composition, capability gaps and future hiring needs.

Team Health

  • Pay attention to engagement, retention, collaboration and emerging people issues across the engineering organisation.

  • Work with Tech Leads when team problems sit somewhere between technical delivery, behaviour and team dynamics.

  • Help maintain a strong remote engineering culture as Stora grows.

Technical Context

  • Stay close enough to the engineering work to understand what the team is solving and the environment they’re working within.

  • Be comfortable reading code, following pull requests and participating intelligently in technical conversations.

  • Partner with Tech Leads without competing with them for technical ownership.

What Success Looks Like

After your first year, we’d expect:

  • Engineers to have a clear understanding of what is expected of them and how they can progress.

  • Managers and engineers to be having better, more useful conversations about performance and development.

  • Performance issues to be addressed early rather than becoming surprises.

  • A progression framework that works for the engineering organisation Stora has become, not the company we were several years ago.

  • Stronger and more consistent hiring and onboarding.

  • The Head of Engineering spending less time acting as the default people manager for the entire engineering organisation.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager, rather than somebody taking their first step into management.

You’ll ideally have:

  • Previous experience directly managing software engineers across more than one team or product area.

  • A strong track record of developing engineers at different stages of their careers.

  • Hands-on experience managing performance, including difficult or underperformance situations.

  • Experience making promotion and progression decisions.

  • Experience running or improving engineering career frameworks, review cycles or progression processes.

  • Previous experience hiring software engineers and building effective interview processes.

  • An engineering background that allows you to understand code and contribute meaningfully to technical conversations.

  • The judgement to know when to get involved and when to leave technical decisions with the Tech Leads.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly in a remote environment.

  • A practical understanding of how AI tools are changing software engineering and experience using them in your own work.

Experience with Ruby or Rails would be useful, but it isn’t essential.

We’re much more interested in whether you can lead engineers well.

What This Role Isn’t

It’s worth being clear that this isn’t:

  • a Tech Lead role with some people management added on;

  • a delivery or project management position;

  • a Product Manager role;

  • a hands-on engineering role where you’ll spend most of your week writing production code;

  • a first Engineering Manager opportunity.

Technical leadership already exists within the product teams.

We’re hiring you because engineering management itself deserves dedicated ownership.

Our Technology

You won’t be expected to spend most of your time writing production code, but you should be comfortable working around our stack.

Backend: Rails, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, TimescaleDB

Frontend: Turbo, React, ViewComponents, Sass

Testing: Minitest, Playwright

Deployment: GitHub Actions, Heroku

Salary & Benefits

  • Salary: Highly competitive and depending on experience

  • Location: Fully remote within the UK or Ireland

  • Belfast office: Available for anyone who wants to use it

  • Private health insurance for you and your family

  • Company pension

  • 35 days’ annual leave inclusive of applicable public/statutory holidays, depending on location

  • Learning and development support

  • Share options

  • Work-from-home budget

Our Hiring Process

We’re reviewing applications as they arrive rather than waiting for a closing date.

If your experience looks like a strong match, we’ll explain the process clearly from the outset and move quickly.

Equal Opportunities at Stora

Stora is an equal opportunities employer.c

We want to build a workplace where people are treated fairly, with dignity and respect, and where different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued.

We welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religious belief or political opinion, or sexual orientation.

Recruitment and employment decisions are based on merit, competence and business need, and we promote equality of opportunity and fair participation in line with our responsibilities under Northern Ireland equality legislation.

If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

We are hiring a Portfolio Partner to own our client book. Our clients are the portfolio: every company raising on Pairs gets a dedicated partner who carries their raise week to week. That partner is you.

Pairs is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients.

The role

You support every company working with us through the life of their raise. You run the weekly calls, keep momentum honest, prepare founders for the investor meetings that matter, debrief what happened, and strategize on an ongoing basis. You also bring a book of your own. Five or more years of relationships with family offices, VCs, HNW investors, and institutional allocators, built and kept warm, now put to work for the companies you manage. This is not a fund seat and you will not manage money. You manage raises and the founders running them. Your hours go to judgment, relationships, and the conversations that keep a raise moving. You report directly to the two co-founders and hold the most client-facing seat in the company.

What you will own

  • A book of client companies: the weekly rhythm, the momentum, and the relationship, from onboarding through close.

  • Investor meetings end to end for your book: prepared before, debriefed after, feedback captured and delivered honestly.

  • Your own investor relationships, worked for the portfolio: the right company in front of the right allocator at the right moment.

  • Raise readiness across your book: narrative, materials, and data room, kept sharp.

  • Renewals earned through ownership: clients stay because the seat works.

You are a fit if you

  • Have 5 or more years across capital markets, private placements, brokerage, or investment management, with direct work on private financings.

  • Hold real, current relationships with family offices, HNW investors, or institutional allocators: when you call, the call gets taken.

  • Have carried companies or clients through a financing personally: the weekly grind, the stalls, and the closes.

What we offer

Fully remote. Your day overlaps with US Eastern time, since that is when your clients and their investors are live. Meetings across the company batch on Mondays and Thursdays; your client rhythm runs on its own cadence. A client-facing seat reporting directly to both co-founders, real ownership of the client book, and relationships that produce visible outcomes.

About us

Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production.

 

Trusted by Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline, and more. We're an ambitious team of 100+ working at the frontier of AI and have raised $60M in Series C funding from Wellington Management, CRV, Next47 and Y Combinator.

 

The role

We're hiring a Learning & Development Specialist in London to design and deliver how Encord teaches the specialist workforce behind its human data — the annotators producing work for frontier AI labs and physical AI companies, in domains such as medical imaging and robotics, and on data types we are running for the first time. How well that workforce is taught is the largest controllable driver of the quality we ship.

You will work at the point where a technical specification becomes something a non-specialist can execute correctly: converting dense, sometimes ambiguous annotation guidelines into instruction a distributed workforce absorbs in days rather than weeks, and into assessment that proves they have.

That teaching problem is a real one, and it is why we are hiring for learning-science expertise rather than for training delivery. The people you teach are capable adults, but they are not domain experts, they come from a wide range of educational backgrounds, and they are frequently working in their second language. Managing cognitive load, breaking a specification into modules that build on each other, leading with worked examples before independent practice, and testing for what actually predicts performance on the job — that craft is the role.

It is a hands-on role. You will design the material and you will stand up and teach it, and it is measured in operational terms: ramp time to competence, first-pass quality, and how much of the workforce is qualified for the work we are selling.


What you'll do

  • Turn a client specification and a set of annotation guidelines into teachable material within days of a project launch — modular, sequenced, and built on worked examples, edge-case libraries and annotated failure cases

  • Design against explicit learning-science principles rather than instinct — manage intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load, chunk a dense specification into modules that build, scaffold then fade support, and use spaced retrieval so what is taught in week one survives to week four

  • Run live training sessions yourself, remotely and to distributed cohorts, daily during a project ramp — and adjust in the room when a concept is not landing

  • Build criterion-referenced assessments that decide readiness rather than test recall, with pass thresholds set alongside the Quality Systems Lead — so that nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard

  • Design for a novice audience by default: no assumed prior knowledge, plain language, and material that works for someone reading in their second language

  • Build durable curricula for the domains we sell repeatedly — medical imaging, document AI, LLM evaluation and red-teaming, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — with progression into higher-skill, higher-rate work

  • Coach the Human Data Program Managers into better teachers: session formats, feedback technique, and observation against a standard, since much of the instruction is delivered by them rather than by you

  • Sit with annotators and watch where they get stuck, then redesign — most of what you need to know is visible in the first hour someone spends on a new task

  • Partner with Product on what belongs inside the Encord platform as guidance at the point of work rather than in a course nobody re-opens

  • Measure every programme against a before-and-after in quality and throughput terms, and retire the ones that do not move an operational number

 

Who we're looking for

  • Grounded in learning theory, and able to say which principle you are applying and why — cognitive load, the worked-example effect, scaffolding and fading, spaced and retrieval practice, criterion-referenced assessment

  • You teach as well as design. You will be in front of a cohort regularly and you are good at it, including when the room is not following you

  • You design for the learner in front of you rather than for someone like yourself — assumed prior knowledge is the most common way training fails here

  • Execution-oriented: a project launching next week needs material this week, and competence in days rather than a term

  • Analytically rigorous. You read quality data and can tell which failures are teachable and which are not, and you are happy being measured on operational metrics rather than completion rates and satisfaction scores

  • You work from a technical specification, and you are often the person who notices the guidelines contradict themselves

  • A clear writer and a strong cross-functional communicator. Most of the workforce you are teaching you will never meet in person

  • Entrepreneurial: this is the first dedicated learning hire here, and you will invent the system rather than inherit one

 

Experience requirements

  • A formal grounding in education, learning science or instructional design — a degree, postgraduate qualification, teaching qualification or equivalent professional training. This is a requirement for this role rather than a preference

  • 3–6 years of professional experience designing and delivering training in an operational environment —where training was measured against production outcomes

  • Demonstrable live facilitation to adult learners, remotely and at cohort scale, not only one-to-one coaching

  • You have built curriculum and assessment from scratch, including assessments that genuinely discriminate between competent and not

  • Experience teaching non-specialist adults, ideally across languages, geographies and levels of prior education

  • Multi-format authoring: written documentation, video, and interactive assessment

  • Comfortable working in data: enough fluency to evaluate your own programmes against quality and throughput reporting

  • Bonus: a classroom or vocational teaching background, or a language-teaching qualification such as CELTA or equivalent

  • Bonus: experience working with teams in India or comparable delivery geographies

Why Encord

  • 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays

The role

We're hiring a Quality Systems Lead to own how Encord measures the quality of the human data we deliver to frontier AI labs, physical AI companies and enterprise AI teams — the standard itself, the systems that evaluate against it, and the audit function that produces the ground truth behind both. Data quality is what our customers buy. As we scale across data types — image and video, document, medical, LLM evaluation, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — quality coverage cannot scale linearly with headcount. So this role has two halves that make each other work. You will build automated evaluation: model-assisted and LLM-based screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output. And you will build and run a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists in India, whose judgements become the labelled ground truth that trains and calibrates that automated layer. As coverage automates, the audit team moves up to the cases models can't judge and to generating gold sets for each new data type we take on. It is an unusual combination — engineering and consistent QC operations in one person — and it is the combination the job needs. You will also have an advantage your counterparts elsewhere in the industry don't: Encord owns the platform this work runs on, so the measurement you build can become native capability in the product rather than internal tooling.

 

What you'll do

  • Build automated dataset quality evaluation and root-cause detection — model-assisted and LLM-as-judge screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output

  • Hire, train, calibrate and manage a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists based in our India operation, held to inter-rater agreement and catch rate rather than volume audited

  • Turn audit output into labelled ground truth that trains and validates the automated layer, and manage the ratio of automated to manual coverage deliberately over time

  • Own the quality standard for every data type we deliver — written rubrics with worked edge cases, golden sets, and acceptance criteria agreed with the customer, alongside the Special Projects lead, before the first batch ships

  • Build scoring systems that rank annotator and reviewer performance and feed routing, staffing and offboarding decisions

  • Set the pass thresholds that certification gates on, so nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard

  • Report quality KPIs to leadership, and into the reporting our Special Projects leads take to customers: accuracy against client spec, inter-annotator agreement, rework rate, cost of rework, and coverage

  • Work with Project Management on remediation — you produce the measurement and the diagnosis, production owns fixing the project, and the standard stays independent of the people being measured

  • Own the unit economics of quality: cost per audited unit, and the coverage you buy per pound spent

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to bring quality measurement into Encord platform as native capability

Who we're looking for

  • You build and you operate. You'll write the evaluation pipeline, and you'll also run the weekly calibration session with ten auditors in another country

  • Your instinct on a coverage problem is to automate it — you reach for a model, a heuristic or a better sampling design before you reach for more auditors

  • Statistically literate in a practical way: sampling design, agreement statistics, and the judgement to spot a metric being optimised against rather than met

  • You can hold a calibrated standard across a distributed team you don't sit with — you know that ten uncalibrated auditors produce ten standards

Fanvue is one of the fastest-growing creator monetisation platforms globally. We're an AI-powered, creator-first platform helping creators connect, engage, and earn directly from their audiences at scale. Following our recent Series A, Fanvue has surpassed $200M+ in annual recurring revenue, with triple-digit year-on-year growth, supporting hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans worldwide.

As Fanvue scales, we need to protect and grow revenue across our mid-to-long-tail creator base without relying on 1:1 CSM ratios. The Pooled CSM model is how we do that: one person owning a large book of creators through data-driven playbooks, automated workflows, and targeted interventions.

🎯 The Role

We're hiring a Pooled Creator Success Manager to own retention and revenue outcomes across a portfolio of 500+ creators in a 1:many, tech-touch model.

This is not a traditional CSM seat. You will not have a handful of named accounts and weekly check-ins. Instead, you will build and run scalable playbooks, monitor risk and contraction signals across a large cohort, and intervene where the data tells you to. Think CS operations meets account management.

You will report to Thea and work closely with the wider Creator Success team.

🚀 What You'll Do

  • Own a pooled book of 500+ creators with full accountability for gross revenue retention

  • Build, maintain, and iterate playbooks that drive retention, reduce contraction, and surface expansion opportunities at scale

  • Monitor creator health signals (engagement drops, earnings decline, support ticket spikes) and run targeted interventions before churn materialises

  • Run a weekly cadence: risk alerts, contraction monitoring, playbook execution reviews

  • Design and automate lifecycle touchpoints (onboarding sequences, re-engagement campaigns, feature adoption nudges) through CS platform workflows

  • Support the broader CS team by providing pooled coverage as more creators move out of dedicated 1:1 management

  • Provide reactive support to creators in the pooled segment when risks, problems, or support needs arise

  • Partner with Product, Support, Moderation, and Growth to close feedback loops and improve creator outcomes

  • Track and report on cohort-level retention, contraction, and engagement metrics

👀 Who You Are

  • Experienced in Customer Success, Account Management, or CS Operations, ideally in a tech-touch or SMB/scale segment

  • Hands-on experience with a CS platform (health scoring, playbook automation, lifecycle workflows)

  • Comfortable building playbooks, automations, and health scores from scratch, not just running someone else's

  • Data-literate: you can pull insights from dashboards, spot trends in cohort data, and translate them into actions

  • Strong written communicator who can craft clear, concise creator-facing messaging at scale

  • Comfortable managing a large book through systems and signals rather than personal relationships

  • Self-directed and structured, you set your own cadence and hold yourself accountable

  • Familiar with the creator economy, subscription platforms, or marketplace models (a plus, not a must)

✨ You'll Thrive Here If

  • You like building systems more than managing relationships one by one

  • You want ownership of a segment, not just a task list

  • You are motivated by retention metrics and commercial outcomes

⚠️ You'll Struggle Here If

  • You prefer deep 1:1 relationships over scaled models

⭐ Fanvue is for Everyone

Talent Acquisition Lead

📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 4 days WFH) | 💰 £60,000 - £70,000

Street Group is scaling fast toward an ambitious growth plan, and hiring is about to get harder: more senior roles, a higher bar, and a market where the best people don't apply; they get found and won. We need someone who owns how we hire, not just who we hire.

We're looking for a TA Specialist with a truly commercial mindset. Skilled at your craft - able to land the hardest hires yourself, but also understanding what will make a whole team better at hiring - from candidate attraction to relationship building; employer brand to candidate experience.

Why this role exists now

Our recruiting team is strong but stacked - and as we get busier, there’s no real capacity to ensure we’re constantly innovating and improving the mechanisms that let us hire quality people at pace. We’ve recently raised investment, and have ambitious goals to achieve - now is the time to fine-tune our recruiting engine so we can scale effectively over the next few years.

The role

This is a role of two halves. The first half is hands-on delivery. IC L5s at Street Group are expected to confidently own the hardest searches - senior roles, niche roles, brand new roles we’ve no experience hiring for. You’ll be expected to understand how the roles you’re hiring for tie in to commercial goals, what to prioritise and why. When you run into issues, you investigate, gather qualitative and quantitative data, conduct market research, and ultimately develop solutions to solve your own problems. You share your knowledge with the team in ways that bring them on the journey - not just the “what and how” but the strong “why” behind it.

The second half is taking our TA function from great to exceptional. Candidate experience, employer brand, AI, tooling, sourcing strategy, assessment - we do all of them well already, but our team holds ourselves to a high standard - and we want to do it all exceptionally well. You’ll collaborate with our Head of People on the most impactful initiatives to prioritise - the what, why, why now, and how it will be achieved and measured. We expect you to be passionate about TA; part of communities, intrigued by industry trends, new tools, best practices, and what other companies are nailing (and making sure we do it even better).

Growth opportunities

The business and People team will grow significantly over the next few years, and there is potential for this role to grow into a management role or specialise in a specific area, but the initial focus and goals will be hands-on, IC L5 work as mentioned above.

Who we're looking for

  • A senior recruiter with deep expertise across the full lifecycle, and the outside-in view: what the market's doing, what great TA teams do, and what it means for us.

  • Someone who holds themselves to a high standard - e.g. measuring their results against quality of hire rather than hires made.

  • Someone whose judgement colleagues calibrate against, trusted with delivering the most senior and confidential searches without a steer.

  • An AI-native mindset: you treat AI as leverage and are keen to learn from our team, and share what’s been working for you.

  • The credibility and communication skills to challenge a department head on a bad hiring decision, deliver hard market news to leadership, and come out with the relationship stronger.

  • Someone who makes the team better on purpose, not by accident: you share what you know and help develop the people around you.

Why you might not want to apply

We'd rather be honest up front, because this role won’t be for everyone.

  • If you want to move into people management now. This is a senior IC role. You'll coach, share knowledge, and set standards, but you won't have direct reports on day one, and you'll still be carrying reqs yourself. If a management title is what you're chasing now or in the imminent future, this isn’t the job for you.

  • If you're a brilliant solo recruiter but you don't have a history of lifting up the people around you. This role will impact how our entire TA function operates, and evidence of knowledge sharing from prior roles will be assessed during the interview process.

  • If AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. We love Claude Cowork, and have both built and used multiple other tools to improve and speed up our ways of working. We have a company-wide expectation that AI is utilised, so it will be a large part of this role.

  • If you tend to report the problems you’re facing in searches. We need someone who spots the funnel stage quietly losing good candidates, or the hiring plan the market won't support, and fixes it before anyone flags it. At IC L5, we don’t expect your manager to be the one flagging problems or coming up with solutions for you.

  • If you like to just crack on with recruitment. Connect with us and join the Talent MCR meetup - we’d love to connect - but this role will be expected to do more than just deliver.

If that list sounds like your kind of role, please apply and let us know why!

We recognise that women and people from underrepresented groups often apply for jobs only when they meet every single requirement listed. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application!

Who are Street Group?

We’re an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother and sister duo, Tom & Heather Staff. Most of us have personal experience of how painful moving can be, and Tom and Heather saw an opportunity to change this: utilising technology, as well as our incredibly talented team, to improve the industry for everyone.

Our products form a powerful duo, working harmoniously together to transform an agent’s job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK.

Back in 2015, our co-Founder, Tom Staff, spent his evenings building Spectre v1.0. He’d seen first-hand an opportunity to automate the very manual process of winning new business for estate agents. Spectre is now our multi-award-winning instruction generation tool, generating an average return on investment for them of over 3000%.

Street.co.uk then launched back in 2020 and serves as our game-changing CRM, allowing agents to deliver a service that aligns seamlessly with the modern, 'on-demand' needs of customers and their busy lifestyles.

Why join Street Group?

🏠 Hybrid-working - you can work from home up to 4 days per week
🏖️ Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!)
💪 Structured career growth and ongoing professional development
📚 £500 yearly L&D budget
🎂 Your birthday on us - we pay, you stay away
🙋 ‘Give something back’ - 2 paid days volunteering on us
👶 Enhanced maternity, paternity & adoption pay
🧠 Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured
🧘 Regular well-being initiatives
🚂 Public transport season ticket loans
🌷 Paid menopause leave
🌞 Holiday buying scheme
🚀 Joining a new team in an exciting business with huge ambition
👥 Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day
👩🏿‍💻 A chance to work on cutting-edge technology
🐶 Comfortable, relaxed office space - office dogs welcome!
🍻 Fully stocked fridge and beers (or an alternative) on us every Friday afternoon
🎊 Company and team off-sites, events and happy hours
🚴 Cycle to work scheme
🚗 Electric car salary sacrifice scheme
🌍 Feel good about sustainability - we're a climate-positive company!

Salary

£60,000 - £70,000, depending on experience. However, sometimes the perfect person is far more or less experienced than we anticipated. In these situations, planned ranges go out the window. If you think that might be the case, please apply and just let us know.


We care deeply about helping the tech industry become a more inclusive and diverse place, and we work hard to lead by example. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a complementary team of employees and building an inclusive environment for all. Candidates must be eligible to live and work in the UK and be able to perform the work specified.

 

Interview Process

3 stages = 60-minute video call with our Head of People > In-person interview with two members of the People team > Final interview with two members of our SLT.

We want to make our interviews as inclusive as possible, so if you need any adjustments made or if there's anything you think we should be aware of during the interview process, please do let us know.

 

A note on using AI in your job application

As a fast-moving and rapidly evolving tech company, we embrace the advantages of AI and encourage its use throughout our application process. However, our goal is to get to know and hire the authentic you - your skills, experience, and values. We don’t want to hire an AI-generated version of you. We consider AI to be a valuable tool, not something that should overshadow you as an individual.

How we use AI in the hiring process

Candidate experience is really important to us, and our Talent team use AI notetakers during interviews so they can focus purely on their conversation with you. All hiring decisions are made by humans - not AI. Let us know if you have any questions!

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone hungry to learn and early in their career to join us as our Revenue Operations Associate!

You'll get an inside look at, and be a key part of, how a high-performing GTM function operates: this is a great opportunity for exceptionally smart, motivated individuals who want to immerse themselves in the world of tech startups and gain real exposure to what it takes to keep a high-growth business moving.

You'll sit at the intersection of our GTM, Customer and Finance teams, keeping our systems, data, and reporting sharp as we scale. This isn't a "keep the lights on" role – you'll inherit processes that are still being built, and you'll have real room to audit what's working, fix what isn't, and put your own stamp on how we operate.

You'll get broad exposure early: one week you might be untangling a HubSpot workflow, the next you're building a dashboard the CCO takes into a board meeting. It's a genuinely excellent grounding in how a B2B SaaS business scales – but it comes with real pace, longer hours than a typical first job, and a learning curve to match. If you want breadth of exposure and a steep climb early in your career, this is a great seat.

What Can You Expect?

  • Keep our GTM tech stack in good shape: Own day-to-day CRM administration – data hygiene, permissions, and workflow upkeep – and support the configuration and integration of the wider stack.

  • Stay ahead of what's new: Keep across releases and new features across our tools – joining release webinars, reading release notes, and flagging what's worth adopting.

  • Help evaluate and set up new tools: Get involved as we add to the stack, from evaluation through to implementation.

data.description:
About Odin

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should be putting it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legals and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why We're Hiring

We're hiring across product, design, engineering, growth, legal and operations - and our US launch will add New York hiring on top of that. Hiring the right people is central to our success to not have someone focused on it entirely.

You'll find exceptional people, but you won't just be the person holding everyone to a bar - you'll work with the founders and leadership team to shape what that bar actually looks like.

This isn't a role where you speak to candidates and move them through a process. You'll understand the product, business and teams deeply enough to assess people properly, challenge hiring managers when needed, and hold the business to the same standard we expect from candidates.

And because you'll often be the first person someone meets from Odin, you'll need to give exceptional people a reason to care about a company many of them haven't heard of yet.

Employer brand is a core part of the role, not something you get to once hiring goes quiet. You'll help build the content, events and community engine that puts Odin in front of the best operators in tech before they're looking for their next job - and makes hiring easier over time.

Responsibilities

  • Run hiring end to end across senior and business-critical roles, from role scoping through to start date.

  • Own pipeline. The people we most want to hire often aren't applying, so outbound, market mapping, network building and getting others involved in referrals are a core part of the week.

  • Run hiring kick-offs that create real clarity around what the role is, what great looks like, and how we're going to assess it.

  • Design interview processes that test reasoning, behaviours and capability rather than rehearsed answers, using challenges, scorecards and structured assessments where appropriate.

  • Own candidate communication end to end, with the same level of care whether someone is progressing or not.

  • Keep employer brand top of mind and be hands-on in shaping it. Whether through content, events or community, you'll find ways to put Odin in front of the right people before they're looking for a job.

  • Use AI as part of how you operate across sourcing, research, screening, candidate experience, operations and employer branding.

  • Use hiring data to change decisions, prioritise roles and coach managers — not simply to report on the funnel.

  • Continuously improve how we use Ashby, our hiring documentation and the quality of our interviews.

  • Give clear, well-reasoned hiring recommendations with limited oversight, including when your view isn't what a hiring manager wants to hear.

Who You Are

  • An experienced recruiter with an unusually high bar for quality and strong judgement across functions. You notice patterns, inconsistencies and signals others can miss, and assess reasoning, behaviours, capability and values rather than relying on experience on paper.

  • Brilliant at asking questions and getting underneath people's reasoning. You surface the questions others are thinking but haven't said out loud, interrogate incomplete briefs, and keep digging until there's real clarity.

  • Comfortable bringing an original point of view rather than simply playing back what's already been said. You'll challenge founders and hiring managers when needed, and do it constructively.

  • Deeply care about candidate experience, even when things are moving quickly, and hold the same bar whether someone is progressing or not.

  • Operationally tight: you spot blockers early, keep processes moving and improve the system while using it.

  • You've used AI in a meaningful way to improve how you hire and can give clear examples of what changed as a result.

Bonus if you have

  • Experience as a first or early Talent hire, where you've had to build structure from scratch.

  • Experience building employer brand or talent marketing that materially changed who engaged with or applied to a company.

  • Experience using hiring funnel or market data to influence decisions, prioritise roles or coach hiring managers.

This role is probably not for you if...

  • You need a lot of structure before you can make progress. There's plenty here still to build, and you'll need to be comfortable creating clarity rather than waiting for it.

  • You avoid making decisions when the context is incomplete. We need someone who can gather the right information, form a view and make high-quality calls without escalating every grey area.

  • You find it difficult to challenge senior stakeholders. You'll need to push back constructively, challenge assumptions and drive clarity with people across the business.

  • You don't enjoy outbound. Proactive pipeline building is a significant part of this role; relying predominantly on inbound won't work here.

  • You tend to take briefs at face value. We want someone who reads between the lines, asks what's missing and brings their own point of view rather than simply executing what they're given.

Bottom line

This isn't about whether you've done 360 hiring before - it's about how you approach it.

We're not looking for someone to simply execute a hiring process. We're looking for a Talent partner who thinks deeply about the role hiring plays in the business, asks excellent questions, brings their own judgement and isn't afraid to challenge when needed.

You'll often be the first person a candidate meets, and you'll have a meaningful influence on how our managers think about hiring.

You're not just moving people through a process. You're helping us decide what great looks like, finding those people, shaping their experience of Odin and raising the quality of how we hire as we grow.

Salary

£70,000–£80,000 + equity options

Working at Odin

We're a London-based team, and this is a role where working closely with the founders and wider team in person makes a real difference.

We move quickly, hiring priorities evolve, and many of the best conversations happen by being close to the teams you're hiring for. We therefore expect this person to be in our London office at least three days per week.

Benefits

  • Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments, and access to Spill for mental health support

  • Wellness: £1,000 annual budget for health, therapy or fitness

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

  • Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

  • Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

  • Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

  • Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

Compensation: £70K – £80K • Offers Equity

data.description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

THE ROLE 

Our brokers play a crucial role in making this a reality. We’re an AI-first business, so whatever the role, we want people who reach for AI by default, stay curious about what it can do, and use it to work faster and think bigger. You’ll use AI day to day, from researching brokers to preparing for meetings, so more of your time goes on the conversations that win business. We’re looking for an ambitious and passionate Broker Development Manager to accelerate our distribution through brokers. In this role, you’ll maximise existing broker relationships and build strong, strategic, growth partnerships as part of our fast-paced distribution team right at the heart of Flock’s mission.

WHAT WE THINK IS MOST EXCITING ABOUT THE ROLE:

Be a part of building something truly game changing in the fleet market. You’ll manage a panel of key strategic brokers with significant growth opportunities. You’ll engage them on the market-leading benefits of Flock’s connected fleet proposition, and how together, we can reduce risk, improve costs and save lives. You’ll also have real freedom in how you use AI to work, whether that’s getting under the skin of a broker’s book before a meeting or spotting growth opportunities across your panel.

A LITTLE MORE ON WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

  • Act as a primary face of Flock for a panel of key broker partners, driving mutual growth and long-term success.

  • Deliver high volumes of broker submissions, directly supporting Flock’s ambitious growth targets.

  • Build, grow and develop our broker panel, onboarding new partners at pace and maximising their commercial potential.

  • Proactively engage brokers, finding new and creative ways to promote Flock’s appetite and proposition as we expand into new sectors.

  • Develop and execute clear, data-driven account growth strategies to drive sustained performance.

  • Achieve strong conversion and retention by supporting day-to-day trading activity and helping brokers (and Flock) win and retain business.

  • Work closely with internal teams, collaborating with brilliant Flockers across the business to deliver shared growth objectives.

  • Maintain strong broker advocacy by being visible, responsive and passionate about Flock’s product, proposition and mission.

  • Use AI in your day-to-day work, from broker research and meeting prep to analysing your pipeline, so your time goes on relationships rather than admin.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK:

ESSENTIAL

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience in managing broker relationships within the insurance sector, possessing a reputable standing in the industry.

  • Energy and innovation in abundance - the ability to work fast, spot opportunity and solve problems. 

  • A proven track record of exceeding revenue targets, driving business growth, and closely collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve collective objectives.

  • An existing network of broker contacts that will enable a rapid integration and immediate impact within Flock’s business development realm.

  • Exceptional understanding of the commercial broker marketplace, competitor carriers, broker business models, and processes.

  • Ability to deliver a consultative sales process, aligning Flock’s value proposition with brokers’ current and future business needs.

  • Comfortable using AI in your daily work, from research and meeting prep to account analysis, and curious about where else it could help you win business.

PREFERABLE

  • Experience building networks of brokers in a Commercial Motor Fleet setting. 

  • Have a broker distribution background with an active panel of brokers in the commercial insurance market. 

  • Can embrace new technologies and products, with experience of successfully distributing these to brokers.

WHAT WE OFFER (in addition to a competitive salary)

  • 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖 

  • Share Incentive Plan 📈

  • Workplace Pension 💰

  • Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

  • Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

  • Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

  • £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

  • £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

  • 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

At Flock, we typically follow a hybrid working model involving a minimum of 3 days per week spent in the office, which is based in Central London, a few minutes walk from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. Please note if your role involves visit to client sites and broker offices, then this can be substituted for office days.

ONE LAST THING..

Authenticity is important to us. We value the unique qualities and experiences you bring. So if you apply, just be your genuine self. It’s who we want!

You'll own the people engine room at Flock: the employee lifecycle, payroll input, benefits, the HRIS, the office and our in-person events. Your job is to design how a modern People function should work at a company where repetitive admin is automated out of existence and every process is simple, scalable and AI-native by default. You'll report to our Senior People Partner and work with everyone here, from a new joiner on day one to the CEO, who cares deeply about our culture.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the full employee lifecycle: contracts, right-to-work, starter and leaver logistics, probations and changes. Shape the first day and first week alongside managers.

  • Be the first point of contact for people queries and audits. Own the People inbox and core HR templates, and drive every query to resolution.

  • Own the HRIS (HiBob) and people data: records, workflows, surveys and data integrity. Deliver monthly People reporting and metrics that spot and close gaps early.

  • Own payroll input end to end: collate, calculate and submit each month, including bonuses and comp changes. Manage the provider and partner with Finance on reporting and year-end.

  • Own benefits end to end as the main contact for providers, systems, data and employee advice, keeping policies and materials current.

  • Run the office environment: building management, health and safety as a trained First Aider and Fire Marshal, and fast hardware provisioning.

  • Own the company social calendar and rituals, from Flock o'Clock to Town Halls and larger events, keeping them engaging and on budget.

  • Cut manual effort across the lifecycle by building AI-native workflows, so every routine people process is automated by default, then coach the business to use them.

  • Partner with IT on joiner and leaver access automation, and on cost and data audits.

What you'll need

  • Hands-on People or HR Operations experience, ideally in a fast-moving scale-up, with real ownership of end-to-end processes. CIPD or equivalent experience required.

  • Hands-on payroll input and benefits administration. HiBob experience is a plus.

  • Strong HRIS skills across workflows, automations and integrations, plus confident data and spreadsheet ability.

  • Real evidence of building with AI: workflows or tools you've shipped and use, not ones you've only read about.

  • Exceptional organisation and judgement. You spot what needs doing and get ahead of it, you build the credibility that lets you influence without leaning on authority, and you treat confidential matters with discretion.

  • A quick, first-principles learner who is comfortable with pace, ambiguity and autonomy.

  • Working knowledge of UK employment law, compliance and people governance.

  • Low ego and high standards. You care most that the work is right and well run.

Our founders spent over a decade at Google shaping the Android operating systems - building and shipping the software that now runs on billions of devices. They didn't just use Android; they led teams responsible for the Android Virtualization Framework, Security, and the Android Runtime (ART).

Through that journey, they saw a quiet but massive crisis: as device software grew in complexity, the tools used to build it remained stuck in the past. Today, a standard Android checkout exceeds 200GB of code, and builds can take hours. This "wait time" is the single biggest tax on innovation.

Source.dev was founded to reimagine software development workflows for device makers. We’re building a new generation of software tools that make building complex device software feel as simple as building a webpage - starting with SourceFS.

The Core Product: SourceFS

SourceFS is a high-performance virtual filesystem designed to turn multi-hour workflows into minutes.

  • 10x Faster Builds: Intelligent caching and virtualization that only materializes files when they are actually needed.

  • 10x Lower Costs: Enabling a standard 16-vCPU machine to outperform even a 128-vCPU machine.

  • True Engineering Productivity: Replaying hundreds of thousands of build steps instantly when inputs match.

The Cultural Anchor: Own It

We operate with a high degree of trust and a shared value of End-to-End Ownership:

"We own our work end-to-end, from spark to finish. It’s about more than just tasks; it’s the dedication to see things through, staying curious to solve problems, thinking from first principles and ensuring we fix our customer’s problems in the best possible way.”

The Role: Pushing the Speed Limits of Rust, Linux & I/O

We are looking for a Performance / Systems Engineer to join us at Source.dev. In this role, your primary metric of success is speed. You will dissect execution paths, eliminate kernel-space context-switching costs, optimize memory layouts, and ensure SourceFS runs as close to the hardware limits as physically possible.

What You’ll Work On

  • System Bottleneck Hunting: Profile, trace, and eliminate latency across CPU, memory, and disk I/O bottlenecks in Rust systems code using tools like perf, eBPF, valgrind, and custom microbenchmarks.

  • Kernel & File System Tuning: Deep dive into Linux kernel interactions, optimizing FUSE drivers, VFS caches, asynchronous I/O (io_uring), memory-mapped execution, and thread scheduling.

  • Memory & Cache Efficiency: Optimize data structures for cache locality, minimize allocation overhead, and eliminate unnecessary memory copies across boundary transitions.

  • Benchmarking Infrastructure: Design robust, reproducible benchmarking suites to measure micro- and macro-performance regression in high-concurrency environments.

  • Scaling Build Primitives: Squeeze peak performance out of massive build graphs (Android, Yocto, and more) running on high-core hardware configurations.

Ideal Candidate Profile:

  • The Performance Systems Mindset: You have a deep understanding of computer architecture (CPU caches, memory barriers, SIMD, system calls) and proven experience writing hyper-optimized code in Rust or C/C++.(or other). No prior experience with Rust required, just a willingness to learn is all we are looking for.

  • Scale-Obsessed: You have experience with (or a burning desire to fix) large-scale build systems and developer tooling.

  • Impact-Driven: You embody the "Own It" mentality - you see a friction point in the developer journey and you don’t stop until it’s gone.

  • Curious & Collaborative: You enjoy translating real-world customer problems into robust, production-grade solutions.

  • Low Ego, High Impact: Beyond being a brilliant coder, you are a thoughtful and empathetic teammate - someone who leads with kindness

  • Feedback Culture Champion: You embrace feedback and provide it thoughtfully; you see open, honest communication as the foundation of great teamwork.

 

A Note on Our Search

We are looking for the best talent, wherever it may be. If you’re on the fence about whether you’re a perfect fit, please do apply - we value diverse backgrounds and unique problem-solving approaches.

Why Join Source.dev?

  • AI-Native Infrastructure: We merge deep systems expertise with AI to solve the "impossible" - using AI to automate complex merges and conflict resolution for the next generation of devices.

  • Architect the Future: Have a direct, visible impact on the infrastructure used to build the world’s most advanced hardware.

  • Early-Stage Ownership: You’ll have a seat at the table to shape our technical roadmap, product direction, and culture from day one.

  • Tier-One Partnerships: Work side-by-side with world-class customers, from global automotive giants to leading cloud providers.

  • Elite Engineering Culture: Join a high-trust & passionate team of engineers

Location: We are currently hiring across key Northern regions and North East coastal hubs. Ideal candidates will be within easy commuting distance of partner EPL and EFL stadiums across these target areas.

Contract Type: Casual hourly contract – Setup Day & Match Day
Hourly Rate: £13.00 - £18.20 Per Hour. Rates vary depending on role

 

Role Overview:

As a Football Tracking Technician, you will work on-site at football stadiums across your region, playing a vital role in the delivery of Hawk-Eye’s tracking and officiating technologies for Premier League, EFL, and UEFA fixtures.

You will be responsible for the setup, calibration, and optimisation of services including Goal Line Technology (GLT) and Electronic Performance & Tracking Systems (EPTS).
